messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: GPU queue depth rising in prod-west (region-us-west-2). Autoscaler attempted scale but failed. Investigating. Threading here for mitigation and handoff.
Aditya: seeing big backlog on inference-queue consumer, token latency spiking >5s for some customers. Grafana: realtime queue length x3 baseline.
Maria: looking at autoscale controller logs — several Failures: 'placementImpossible' and 'InsufficientMIGSlots'. Looks like MIG slicing mismatch; many nodes have small leftover slices that can't host requested pod shapes.
Aditya: confirmed. kubectl describe shows Pending pods with reason 'FailedScheduling', events:
```
FailedScheduling: 0/48 nodes are available: 28 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 20 NoSuitableMIG.
```
Aditya: autoscaler reported attempted provisioning 6 new instances but AWS quota OK. The provider returned nodes but kube-scheduler refused due to strict MIG sizing and packing constraints.
Devon: @Aditya can you paste the autoscaler error lines?
Aditya: logs: "scale_up.go: schedule failed, compatible node templates exhausted; bundling request to fallback-config returned capacity but mismatch in MIG topology"
Jess: quick customer impact: two enterprise tenants seeing 429s on generation and embedding jobs delayed. Estimated ~1200 requests queued, P99 latency ~12s. Marking SEV-2 for now.
Kevin: I'm on-call and on the call. Short-term mitigation options: 1) relax MIG affinity to allow pods on smaller slices, 2) manual repack (drain specific nodes and restart to defragment), 3) burst to Dedicated reserved pool (if available) as fallback.
Maria: relaxing affinity requires config change in scheduler policy and will risk noisy-neighbor perf for some heavy models. But it will accept pods. Suggest manual repack first to reclaim stranded slices.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty triggered to current oncall Kevin (ack id PD-8842).
SRE Pager: Kevin acknowledged the page.
Kevin: starting repack plan: identify nodes with stranded GPU capacity (MIG fragments < required). Command I'm running: `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, migSlices: .status.allocatable["nvidia.com/mig-slice"]}'`
Maria: helpful. I'm running a script to map pods -> MIG capability: `python tools/mig_map.py --namespace=inference --output=map.csv`
Devon: prepping a manual scale-up request to cloud to temporarily add 8 x p4d nodes under emergency pool. Request queued with infra-ops (ticket INFRA-5226). If cloud can add nodes with different MIG configs we can schedule the large pods there.
Aditya: also enabling prefix caching to reduce token count for queued requests temporarily (config toggle). Should reduce demand by ~20%. Doing rollout to 10% of routes.
Jess: Notifying affected account owners via account ops. Drafted message: "We are experiencing higher-generation latency due to GPU allocation constraints; mitigation in progress."
Kevin: mitigation step 1 (now): start draining three nodes with highest fragmentation, cordon & drain non-critical pods, then trigger `repack` daemon to recreate optimal MIG distribution. This will cause short-lived evictions but should free usable slices.
Maria: I will update repack parameters to prefer larger contiguous allocations: `--prefer-contiguous --max-surge=2`
Kevin: performing drain on node gpu-az2-12 now: `kubectl drain gpu-az2-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Aditya: moved some lower priority batch jobs to backlog, reduced concurrency on retrain tasks.
SRE Pager: @Devon you're next for the handoff at +30m. Please monitor scaling tickets and customer comms.
Devon: Roger. I'll take over after Kevin's repack finishes.
IncidentBot: Note: autoscaler metrics show throttle on scale operations due to placement fragment checks — recorded in incident log 4205552468-ops.log
Maria: after repack (estimate 8-12m) we'll attempt a controlled autoscale test: synthetic workload to confirm new packing works.
Jess: customers updated. Support channel open for priority customers.
Kevin: repack completed on nodes gpu-az2-12/13/14. Observed reclaimed 6 MIG slices, scheduler accepted 4 previously pending pods. Queue length dropped ~35%.
Aditya: good progress. Autoscaler now succeeded in provisioning 2 more nodes to meet demand. No new FailedScheduling errors in last 5m.
Devon: taking over. Next actions: monitor P99 latency, confirm no regressions in throughput, follow up with infra to create ticket for MIG sizing audit (INFRA-5227). Also propose adding a small buffer in autoscaler for fragmented regions.
Maria: postmortem notes for later: root cause likely aggressive MIG slicing defaults + binpack policy that prevented using partial capacity. Action items: evaluate default MIG sizes, improve scheduler fallback to allow temporary mixed-MIG placement, add repack automation during low-traffic windows.
Jess: tagging incident as SEV-2 -> downgrade to SEV-3 observed improvement but keeping channel open until stable.
SRE Pager: Handoff complete to Devon. Kevin, please stay available for 30m if rollback needed.
Devon: acknowledging. I'll update `#incidents` with status every 10m.
IncidentBot: Incident closed to paging but thread remains for notes. Final impact: transient latency spikes for 2 enterprise customers, no data loss, estimated 30 minutes total degraded window.
Jess: adding final followup: schedule a runbook update and a postmortem in docs. Assigning owners: Maria -> root cause investigation, Aditya -> mitigations automation, Devon -> autoscaler policy changes.
Kevin: thanks all, great coordination. :thumbsup:
